title: Adaptive config guardrails and cost-surge analysis for Optimize auto-tuner
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Follow-up ticket to define non-invasive guardrails and an analysis framework after a recent Optimize auto-tuner event produced a transient cost spike. This work bundles a short-term containment checklist, a reproducible simulation harness for candidate config changes, and a proposal for a signal-driven canary gating mechanism before any config apply at scale.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-20 an automated recommendation from the Optimize tuner pushed a set of batching and prefix-cache parameter changes to ~22% of Dedicated customers in a staged rollout. Within 35 minutes we observed a 42% increase in per-token GPU utilization and a 31% uplift in infra spend on impacted pools. There were no customer-facing errors but some customers reported higher throttling and higher latency percentiles. The staged rollout aborted automatically after the detect-and-hold sentinel triggered at 40% cost delta.
timeline:
2026-02-20 08:12 UTC: Autotuner generated recommendations for batch_window_ms and kv_cache_ttl.
2026-02-20 09:05 UTC: Canary apply started to 10% pools.
2026-02-20 09:37 UTC: Observability flagged sustained GPU utilization increase and bursty queueing; cost delta > 25%.
2026-02-20 09:40 UTC: Sentinel 'cost-delta-hold' activated; rollout paused.
2026-02-20 10:10 UTC: Engineers launched targeted dry-run replay for the affected workload to gather trace-level evidence.
2026-02-20 12:30 UTC: Rollback completed to previous config across canaries.
2026-02-21 14:00 UTC: Initial incident review; hypothesis formed around mispredicted batch shape distribution and stale sequence-length histogram used by the tuner.
2026-02-28 16:00 UTC: This follow-up ticket opened to define mitigations and a simulation harness.
root_cause: The autotuner relied on an outdated sample of request sequence-length distribution (collected 72 hours earlier) combined with a heuristic that favored aggressive batching under low observed variance. A recent customer traffic pattern change introduced frequent long-history chat sessions which amplified KV cache churn and increased GPU memory pressure; the tuner suggested larger batch sizes that increased serialization overhead and disrupted kernel selection heuristics, producing a non-linear cost increase.
short_term_mitigations: Reinstate conservative default caps: enforce max_delta_cost = 15% for any staged apply until new validation gating is in place.
Turn on sequence-length freshness requirement: reject recommendations that rely on histograms older than 2 hours.
Add an emergency fast-revert API for Optimize applies with 1-click rollback and telemetry snapshotting.
Create a temporary throttle to limit autotuner apply velocity to <= 5% of pools per hour.
long_term_actions: Build a deterministic simulation harness that replays live traffic samples against candidate batch/cache configs in an isolated compute environment and produces cost/latency delta estimates before apply.
Introduce a multi-signal canary gate that requires (a) simulated cost delta < 10%, (b) per-pool simulated latency P95 delta < 8%, and (c) no kernel fallback rate changes beyond historical variance.
Augment tuner feature set with 'sequence-length skew' metric and carry-forward uncertainty estimates; prefer conservative suggestions when uncertainty is high.
Integrate anomaly-aware historical baselining so applies compare to similar workload clusters rather than global averages.
testing_plan:
1) Implement simulation harness and run 72-hour backfill across 10 representative clusters (small, medium, large).
2) Create synthetic long-history chat traces and validate harness sensitivity to KV-cache churn.
3) Run A/B dry-runs where candidate configs are applied to duplicated traffic in staging to validate the canary gate thresholds.
4) Automate smoke checks post-apply that verify cost and latency deltas at 1h, 6h, and 24h windows.
All results recorded in the 'Optimize Simulation' Confluence space and linked PRs.
runbook_changes: Add new section 'Optimize: pre-apply simulation checklist' with required artifacts (simulation report, kernel fallback histogram, recommended max_delta_cost).
Add decision matrix for emergency rollback that lists who can authorize immediate revert (SRE lead + Optimize owner).
Document the new fast-revert API usage and telemetry preservation steps for postmortem analysis.
